reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about amorphization, dislocation pileup, and a creep mechanism transition in HEA multilayers, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover these specific behaviors in this novel material system.
premises: Semicoherent interfaces in FCC/BCC HEA multilayers cause localized stress-induced interfacial amorphization under sustained loading.
Dislocation pileup at misfit dislocations drives this amorphization.
Amorphization lowers atomic-migration barriers, enabling a transition from dislocation-mediated to diffusion/interface-slip-mediated creep.
This transition results in enhanced creep resistance (lower stress exponent n ~ 1–2) compared to coherent or grain-boundary-dominated interfaces (n > 3).
Coherent interfaces (8 nm) transmit dislocations easily, while grain-boundary-dominated structures (32/80 nm) undergo primarily dislocation-mediated creep.
